title.en: Watermill wheel, transmission and working load

summary: Connect a waterwheel to a readable transmission and working machine, keeping the water representation separate from the chosen drive model.
objective: Let a viewer follow the drive from water admission through a supported wheel shaft to a visible useful output and see how controls alter that chain.
intent_signals: connect water flow control to working machinery
example_prompts: Build a mill cutaway where a wheel drives a shaft, transmission and grain-handling mechanism.
Design a fictional watermill with meaningful stop and restart states, while labeling its motion as illustrative.

principles: The cited Peirce Mill example connects wheel rotation through a shaft to gears, belts, an elevator and machinery. Use that complete power-chain idea without copying undocumented ratios or claiming every mill has the same layout.
Separate water admission, wheel/shaft rotation, transmission and working load. Give every rotating axis a visible support and every output a declared connection.
Choose wheel type and entry/exit path together. An invented paddle or bucket layout is acceptable, but the depicted water path should explain where the authored driving action is applied.
A flow control may drive an illustrative speed response; it is not automatically a calculation of hydraulic power, inertia, torque or grain throughput.
implementation: Create millrace/flume, gate, wheel rim/spokes and paddles or buckets, axle, two bearing housings, transmission stages and output machine as named groups. Show water entry and a downstream exit without moving the base water volume merely to convey flow.

Place wheel geometry around the actual shaft pivot. Attach rigidly joined hubs to that shaft; keep stationary bearing housings outside its rotating group. Make transmission axis changes visible with a chosen gear or belt arrangement.

For an illustrative drive, store gate opening, target speed, actual displayed speed, drive phase and optional disengagement state. Use bounded acceleration/deceleration and derive all coupled part phases from one authoritative drive phase with declared authored ratios and sign conventions.
If the visual includes teeth or a belt, inspect the contact region: use matched geometric motion or clearly schematic pitch wheels. Do not independently spin downstream parts at unrelated clocks.

Give the working output a visible consequence such as a rotating runner stone, a reciprocating linkage or moving elevator buckets. Treat grain particles and production counters as schematic unless supported by a transport model.

Offer gate, stop/resume and transmission cutaway controls. Decide whether disengagement is modeled before exposing it, and reset wheel phase, output state, gate setting and display timers consistently.
observable_checks: A slow rotation shows wheel and shaft remaining attached while bearing housings stay fixed.
Zero commanded drive brings the authored coupled machinery to its declared rest behavior; downstream parts do not continue from an independent animation clock.
The cutaway reveals a continuous named chain to the output rather than a shaft ending inside an unexplained wall.
Stop midway, resume and reset: coupled phases remain consistent and no extra work count appears during pause.

known_limits: Historical source supports the Peirce Mill power-chain description, not this fictional layout, gear ratios or waterwheel efficiency.
Schematic speed response, decorative water marks and particles are not a hydraulic or grain-processing simulation.
Authored modeling guidance and prospective checks; no runtime artifact has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Choose undershot, overshot, horizontal or explicitly fantastical wheel forms with a coherent authored water path; vary scale, enclosure and transmission visibility.

claims.statement: The NPS Peirce Mill panel describes water turning a wheel whose shaft drove gears, belts, a grain elevator and other machinery.
claims.scope: Documented Peirce Mill interpretation; no universal mill configuration or quantitative power claim.

source_refs.locator: Interpretive panel transcript, paragraph beginning Peirce Mill represents: wheel, shaft, gears, belts and grain elevator.
